canonical_name: Transmission Control Protocol — RFC 9293 consolidated living standard

standardized.notes: RFC 9293 consolidates the RFC 793 lineage and later normative updates.

last_known_use.notes: TCP remains a core Internet transport protocol.

addressing: Transport ports combined with IP-layer addressing identify communication endpoints/flows.
routing_or_forwarding: No routing function; carried by IP.
error_control: Sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and checksum-based protection support reliable ordered transport.
flow_or_congestion_control: Receiver-window flow control is part of the core lineage; congestion-control mechanisms were added and evolved in later branches and are not reducible to the 1981 RFC alone.

survival.provenance_notes: Protocol identity survives while the normative standards document was consolidated from RFC 793 and decades of updates into RFC 9293.

open_questions: Map every RFC incorporated/obsoleted by RFC 9293 to exact TCP mechanisms.
Separate congestion-control branches from the base protocol specification.
Correlate BSD/Linux implementation revisions with standards revisions.

supports: explicit decades-long evolution and incorporation of RFC 793 functional specification

notes: Reference example of obsoleted-document-living-protocol continuity: RFC 793 is obsolete, but its protocol lineage is directly incorporated into RFC 9293.
